Subject: Post-call recap & TCO next steps (Acme)

Hi Jordan / Sasha 

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps we agreed on. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Token bill variability across peak traffic and multi-turn conversations (primary concern).
- Latency SLOs for interactive support use cases (target <250ms p95).
- Ops friction around model updates and rollout risk to production.
- Budget constraint: ~USD 60k / quarter target for inference costs for the pilot.

Goals you shared:
- Reduce per-session inference cost by 30-40% vs current vendor through batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantized model variants.
- Maintain sub-250ms p95 for the majority of user flows.
- Run a 6-8 week pilot (50k monthly sessions) to validate cost and latency improvements.

TCO levers we discussed (high level):
1) Batching & concurrency tuning  reduces per-token compute by increasing GPU utilization for non-latency-critical backfill and bulk inference.
2) Prefix/KV caching  very effective for conversational reuse (saves tokens on repeated prompts).
3) Model tiering / fallbacks  route low-criticality traffic to smaller quantized models while keeping high-fidelity models for important flows.
4) Memory-optimized kernels / quantization  model-specific quantization profiles can reduce GPU cost 2-3x with controlled quality decline.

Next steps (action items & owners):
- Marissa: share a preliminary TCO estimate and one-pager on recommended levers (attached).
- Rafael: schedule a technical deep-dive to validate latency and KV caching integration (suggest Tues/Thu next week).
- Jordan / Sasha: confirm pilot scope and budget band (are you ok with $45k$60k / quarter target for the pilot?).

Attachments: acme-tco-estimate.xlsx (prelim numbers), redwood-cost-levers-one-pager.pdf

Best,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa  helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: we have flexibility up to $60k/quarter for the pilot, but would prefer to land closer to $45k if the quality/latency targets can be met.
- Traffic profile: ~50k sessions/month, ~3.2 turns per session on average; 40% of sessions are high-priority (support reps), 60% are async user-facing flows.
- Latency: the sub-250ms p95 target is for the high-priority flows only. For async flows we can accept up to 1s.

Can Rafael confirm whether KV/prefix caching would realistically cover the 40% high-priority traffic reuse patterns you saw in the demo? If not, we need to understand the expected savings window.

Also  we'll be pulling procurement once we lock the pilot budget; expect cross-functional review (security & finance).

Hi Jordan  quick technical note on caching behavior.

Short answer: yes, KV/prefix caching can cover a meaningful portion of the 40% high-priority reuse, but the exact savings depend on prompt entropy and how much of the prompt body is stable (e.g., system + initial user context). From similar customers we've seen: 
- If ~30-50% of token volume is stable prefixes, caching can reduce token usage by ~20-35%.
- Combined with batching on lower-priority async flows and a quantized model for non-critical routes, overall cost reductions of 30-45% are achievable in our pilots.

For the technical deep-dive I'll bring sample cache hit-rate benchmarks and a proposed config (prefix length, TTL, eviction) so we can model expected savings for your traffic. Suggested slots: Tue 25 May 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 27 May 14:00-15:00 PT.
